summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the season-ending decision arrives inside an ordinary work morning. Middle image: the review deadline competes with real tasks. Closing image: the temporary bracket keeps the abstract future physically grounded.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning in operations: Astra opens the program-disposition review while still sorting ordinary work orders.
PANEL 2 — The review deadline sits on the same desk as the day's actual work; Pixa states that the recommendation window closes in four hours.
PANEL 3 — Zib arrives carrying the temporary-bracket inspection tag and a real wrench, bringing the unresolved physical need into the review.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks from the future-of-site packet to the repair still holding part of the station together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Central review needs a final disposition for Stardust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Disposition. It sounds like a word someone uses when they don't want to say closing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Before anyone closes anything, tell them the bracket is still temporary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I intend to. That part of the station remains unusually eloquent.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the disposition review. Opening image: central review defines the available institutional futures. Middle image: none describe Stardust as it actually operates. Closing image: Astra chooses to construct a fourth option rather than select a false one.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The packet lays out Option One: dedicated material pilot, increased budget, priority procurement, required output targets.
PANEL 2 — Option Two offers low-priority operations with pilot support ending; Option Three offers consolidation and site closure.
PANEL 3 — Jax reads the three-option menu while Glorp scrolls for a standard fourth choice and finds none.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks at the three boxes and decides that the missing option is now the work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Option one makes us a material pilot with an output quota.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Option two keeps us operating until the pilot money disappears. Lovely choices.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Option three closes the station. There isn't a fourth box.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then we'll have to write one. That's the work now.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the tempting standard option is tested against the exact repair need that drove the season. Middle image: the temporary fix remains sound but unresolved. Closing image: Astra refuses to let the metric replace the repair need even before anyone proposes the bargain.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the maintenance bay, Zib opens the coolant-balancing unit while Astra brings the review slate with her.
PANEL 2 — The approved clamp still carries the structural load while Mira checks the old material record beside the live inspection.
PANEL 3 — REPLACEMENT PART ETA: 12 DAYS sits beside Option One's priority-procurement promise on Astra's slate.
PANEL 4 — Zib notices Astra looking between them and rejects the bargain before she can voice it; Astra says she knows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: This repair works with the ordinary brace. The sample helps fill one gap. It isn't a new station function.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: It's still an interesting physical result. You don't have to make it sound embarrassed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Can we test how often this would replace a real part?

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Not honestly, no. I wouldn't bet a building on it. I might bet a spare washer.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing the bracket inspection. Opening image: Astra rejects the provided framing physically. Middle image: the fourth option begins as a handwritten evidence question. Closing image: the crew's proof standard is established before the proposal exists.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra closes the standard-options slate and sets it face-down beside the inspection tools.
PANEL 2 — On the back of an ordinary work-order sheet she writes WHAT CAN WE PROVE? and Mira draws OPERATIONS / MATERIAL beneath it.
PANEL 3 — Astra looks out toward the working station and asks for defensible evidence rather than pitch language.
PANEL 4 — Brick opens his notebook enthusiastically; Astra specifies evidence they can defend, and Brick closes it again while Zib keeps working.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: They've given us three options and none is the place I manage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Then put operations on one side and the material on the other. Don't make them sound like the same job.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: What can we prove?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: I have notes on the station's persistent mysteries.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Start with the repair records. They're much less mysterious.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Back in operations, Astra and Pixa move through the working level while normal jobs continue around them. Middle image: Pixa answers while moving with them. Closing image: Pixa adds the plain operational fact without interpretation.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, Astra and Pixa move through the working level while normal jobs continue around them; Pixa calls out only measures tied to visible work.
PANEL 2 — Jax closes an access route behind a finished task as Pixa notes incident detection time and accepted local ownership.
PANEL 3 — Zib closes a service panel as Pixa notes repair closure and repeat-incident rate. Astra checks the measurement boundary.
PANEL 4 — Pixa answers while moving with them.
PANEL 5 — Mira stops at the cargo-delay entry and points at it.
PANEL 6 — Pixa adds the plain operational fact without interpretation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: I've collected the ordinary maintenance history and response records.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: How much of this looks like the last year?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: All of it. Most of it was inconvenient when it happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: And some of the inconvenient days gave us the samples.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Don't let that be a reason to schedule more inconvenient days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: We tried that. I still owe Dock Two an apology.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the station's accumulated work history enters as physical evidence. Middle image: operational mess and material uncertainty are placed side by side. Closing image: Zib identifies a repeatable outcome without inventing a new metric.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib rolls the stained work board into the review area, full of mundane closed jobs from across the season.
PANEL 2 — Astra studies the crossed-out notes, magnets and repaired items and calls the board ugly.
PANEL 3 — Zib points to the closed column and calls it work while Mira holds the equally messy material chart beside it.
PANEL 4 — Zib points to the open-work column and identifies the operational number Stardust actually knows how to reduce.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Here's the repaired bracket, the failed checks, and the work we did around the delay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: None of it glamorous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: But it's actual evidence. We had a problem, tested options, and kept the station working.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: And occasionally complained with great skill. Please include that under local expertise.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: the material history is physically reviewed without romanticizing it. Middle image: uncertainty itself becomes part of the evidence. Closing image: Mira authors the boundary that the final program must preserve.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At the lab bench, Mira lays the season's retained samples in physical order from brittle fragments to the limited-use filler.
PANEL 2 — Short test cards beside them make the material limits visible: variable properties, inconsistent yield, mass not predictive, mechanism unresolved.
PANEL 3 — Astra asks what can actually be promised; Mira answers collection and characterization, nothing stronger.
PANEL 4 — Mira writes NO INFERRED EMOTIONAL FIELDS herself and Astra tells her to keep the wording exact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: This sample held twice and failed when we changed the temperature. I'm not hiding either result.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: You still love it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Of course I do. Some of my favorite things are questions we haven't answered.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then our report should leave you room to keep asking, without promising the answers in advance.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Cargo Bay / Dock 2. Opening image: the season's clearest failure is revisited in the place where it happened. Middle image: Jax connects motive to operational consequence. Closing image: Astra converts her mistake into evidence for the fourth option.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the cargo lane, Jax stops Astra beside the conveyor they serviced early and opens the route history.
PANEL 2 — He traces the accelerated conveyor closure into the Dock 2 delay while the actual lane remains visible behind them.
PANEL 3 — Jax states the operational lesson plainly: when collection became the reason for the job, the real route got worse.
PANEL 4 — Astra accepts responsibility without defense and tells Jax to put that evidence into the review packet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: This is where the conveyor blocked the dock when we moved a service job early.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I remember.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I know. I just wanted to be sure the report remembers it too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: It will. And when the next ship comes in, I'll listen when you tell me what the schedule means.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Back in operations, Glorp spreads the actual sample labels, custody slips and local disclosure cards across a desk while Kreeb removes individual personal text. Middle image: Glorp looks at the empty area. Closing image: Glorp stamps the form: BEHAVIORAL CONTEXT: NOT REQUIRED.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, Glorp spreads the actual sample labels, custody slips and local disclosure cards across a desk while Kreeb removes individual personal text before anything is copied forward.
PANEL 2 — Glorp writes the required operational fields on a clean form: owner; task; physical condition; chain of custody; unresolved questions.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb leaves deliberate physical space beneath them for optional disclosure and writes: no behavioral condition required; intentional blank permitted.
PANEL 4 — Glorp looks at the empty area.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb looks at the blank paper too.
PANEL 6 — Glorp stamps the form: BEHAVIORAL CONTEXT: NOT REQUIRED.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: They want an owner, task, condition and chain of custody. That much we can record.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: And they don't need a field for what someone was thinking while it happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: I'm leaving a blank for context that people actually choose to share.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Can we also leave it empty if nobody chooses?

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I had to sit with that idea for a while, but yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Behavioral context: not required. I rather like writing that.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the evidence assembly. Opening image: the different proof streams finally occupy one physical frame. Middle image: the fourth option receives a name through ordinary editing. Closing image: the crew accepts language as a tool rather than an identity.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib's work board, Jax's route slate, Mira's sample cards and Glorp/Kreeb's reporting form now surround WHAT CAN WE PROVE? on one workbench.
PANEL 2 — Astra writes ADAPTIVE OPERATIONS / INCIDENTAL MATERIALS OBSERVATION as the first rough heading.
PANEL 3 — Mira catches the plural; Astra crosses out the S instead of defending it.
PANEL 4 — Zib complains that the phrase still sounds like a department.
PANEL 5 — Astra accepts the temporary institutional language because today the station needs something central review can carry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: This packet has the station's work history on one side and the material tests on the other.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Good. Now nobody can confuse a sample with a replacement bracket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: They're still going to ask whether we can make more.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then we tell them we don't know. I think we've earned the right to be boring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: You can be boring. Mira and I have interesting repairs to finish.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra folds the sheet into two literal sections: PRIMARY FUNCTION / SECONDARY OBSERVATION. Middle image: Mira adds in ink: NO OUTPUT TARGET. Closing image: Pixa reads the whole physical packet before it is digitized.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra folds the sheet into two literal sections: PRIMARY FUNCTION / SECONDARY OBSERVATION.
PANEL 2 — Under Primary she writes: STATION OPERATIONS / ADAPTIVE RESPONSE / MAINTENANCE CLOSURE, then clips Zib's work-order evidence beneath it.
PANEL 3 — Under Secondary Mira writes: PASSIVE MATERIAL COLLECTION / PHYSICAL CHARACTERIZATION, then sets one sealed sample card beneath it.
PANEL 4 — Mira adds in ink: NO OUTPUT TARGET.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb adds beside the intentional blank: NO BEHAVIORAL CONDITIONS.
PANEL 6 — Pixa reads the whole physical packet before it is digitized.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Primary function: operating and maintaining Stardust. Secondary observation: collecting and testing incidental material.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Say the material can be useful under tested conditions. Not that it always will be.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: And no one has to perform an emotion to make the pilot work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: There. No output target.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: The two parts of the report now agree with the work history.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: An unusual luxury.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the fourth-option review. Opening image: the proposal reaches the credible outside advocate. Middle image: the Liaison resists the category, not the station. Closing image: Astra grounds the case in evidence rather than exceptionalism.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Operations Liaison joins by live call while Astra sends the fourth recommendation.
PANEL 2 — The Liaison reads silently long enough for the crew to wait instead of pitching over them.
PANEL 3 — The Liaison lowers the tablet and states the central problem: this is not a standard pilot category.
PANEL 4 — Astra answers that the operating record—not Stardust's uniqueness—is the argument, and the Liaison keeps reading.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: I read the fourth option. It's unlike the categories central offered.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I know. But it's the station you've visited.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: You'll have to explain why operations deserve the budget without a promised material output.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I'm planning to explain the same thing we showed you in the corridor.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The Liaison reaches the budget comparison. Middle image: The bracket ETA sits open on a side screen. Closing image: Astra looks at the crew around the table. Nobody tells her what to choose.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Liaison reaches the budget comparison.
PANEL 2 — On the live call, the Liaison points to the budget comparison on the shared review screen.
PANEL 3 — Astra knows exactly what that buys.
PANEL 4 — The bracket ETA sits open on a side screen.
PANEL 5 — The Liaison continues.
PANEL 6 — Astra looks at the evidence gathered around the table. Nobody answers for her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: Option one offers faster parts and a larger material budget.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: And we'd be expected to produce a quantity we can't predict.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: Correct. Option four gives you a defensible operating budget, but fewer guarantees.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That bracket is still waiting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: I know why the faster route is tempting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: So do I. We tried moving our jobs around a target once.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the live review. Opening image: the decision is made explicit rather than implied by drafting. Middle image: Astra physically chooses the fourth option. Closing image: she accepts the institutional risk without turning it into heroism.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Liaison asks which recommendation Astra actually wants carried forward; the three standard options and the handwritten fourth remain visible together.
PANEL 2 — Astra slides the standard options aside and centers the fourth recommendation: recommend the station we actually run.
PANEL 3 — The Liaison warns that this option can lose; Astra leaves it unchanged and says she knows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: Which option are you asking me to recommend?

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: The fourth. The station we actually run, not a factory we hope to become.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: I can take it forward. I can't promise it'll win.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I wouldn't trust you if you could.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Central review returns written questions while the Liaison remains on the call. Middle image: Question: WHAT MATERIAL YIELD CAN BE COMMITTED?. Closing image: Question: THEN WHY RETAIN MATERIAL OBSERVATION? Mira looks at Astra. Astra lets her answer.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Central review returns written questions while the Liaison remains on the call.
PANEL 2 — Question: WHAT IS THE REPRODUCIBLE OUTPUT?
PANEL 3 — Astra answers.
PANEL 4 — Question: WHAT MATERIAL YIELD CAN BE COMMITTED?
PANEL 5 — Mira answers.
PANEL 6 — Question: THEN WHY RETAIN MATERIAL OBSERVATION? Mira looks at Astra. Astra lets her answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: Central has returned questions. They're not quite ready to reject this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Reproducible output? The work record. Repairs, response times, service kept running.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: And what material yield can you promise?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: None. We have a physical observation, with limits. You can't schedule it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then why keep observing it? Mira, that's your question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Because sometimes science is worth doing before anyone knows what to buy from it.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: central review demands compression. Middle image: the answer is authored by the ensemble rather than summarized for them. Closing image: the season's operational and human boundaries become one value statement.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Central review asks for one concise value statement; Astra starts typing and stops.
PANEL 2 — She turns to the crew and asks for the plain answer instead of writing a management version herself.
PANEL 3 — Zib anchors the answer on the stained work board: we keep the place working.
PANEL 4 — Mira adds that they measure the strange part without pretending to understand it; Glorp adds that the record can prove both.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb taps the intentional blank and completes the statement: the proof does not require people to become records while Astra types.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: They want one statement of value. I'm trying not to write it like a conference banner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: We keep the place working. That's what people call us for.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: And we test the unusual things we find without pretending they know how we feel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: We can document both honestly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: And people can still be people when they aren't being measured.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the review. Opening image: the unapproved fourth option sits beside the sanctioned choices. Middle image: the institutional cost is stated one last time. Closing image: Astra chooses before knowing whether the choice will be rewarded.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra submits the fourth site recommendation with the three standard choices still displayed beside it.
PANEL 2 — The Liaison asks one final time whether she is declining the safer dedicated-material recommendation.
PANEL 3 — Astra answers that they have a fourth and presses SUBMIT before any approval exists.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: There. Fourth recommendation submitted.

dialogueInline.speaker: Operations Liaison
dialogueInline.text: Are you declining the dedicated-material option? It would be easier to defend.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Easier for the report. Harder for every person who has to work here. That's my answer.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the major decision produces no immediate answer. Middle image: the station resumes the work that existed before the review. Closing image: Jax's learned routine continues while the future remains pending.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — UNDER EVALUATION appears as Astra returns from the review to the still-open bracket panel.
PANEL 2 — Zib immediately puts the decision back in scale by handing her the work in front of them.
PANEL 3 — Astra joins the scheduled bracket inspection while Jax picks up the monitoring reader without being assigned.
PANEL 4 — Zib asks for the remembered six-minute interval and Jax confirms it with familiar annoyance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: The decision hasn't arrived. The bracket has still arrived zero times.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I can check the monitoring interval. It's better than standing around refreshing a screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I'll take the next work order.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Good. We had a station before they made a category for us.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Montage across Stardust Station's ordinary working spaces during the pending review: maintenance bay, lab work area, quiet-room threshold and operations level. Opening image: Over the next stretch of the shift, the station keeps operating while the review remains pending; Zib and Jax continue the active bracket inspection. Middle image: Kreeb returns the quiet-room chairs after someone borrowed them. Closing image: Astra glances once at the pending review on a distant screen, then turns the screen away and takes the work order. She does not refresh it again.
settingText: Montage across Stardust Station's ordinary working spaces during the pending review: maintenance bay, lab work area, quiet-room threshold and operations level.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Over the next stretch of the shift, the station keeps operating while the review remains pending; Zib and Jax continue the active bracket inspection.
PANEL 2 — Mira checks the temporary material filler at the actual repair and records only its physical condition. No new claim.
PANEL 3 — Glorp closes an ordinary safety record at a working counter.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb returns the quiet-room chairs after someone borrowed them.
PANEL 5 — Pixa reports routine uptime while passing Astra a normal work order that needs attention.
PANEL 6 — Astra glances once at the pending review on a distant screen, then turns the screen away and takes the work order. She does not refresh it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Still holding. And the replacement still hasn't appeared.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: You might miss the pleasure of being annoyed with procurement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: The material filler remains unchanged. I wish I had something new to tell you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Safety record closed. Nobody's asked me to describe the emotional conditions.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: I put the quiet-room chairs back. Someone borrowed both of them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Astra, ordinary service order. It isn't waiting for central's answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then that gets done first.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the answer arrives without fanfare. Middle image: the fourth option is accepted with its crucial boundaries intact. Closing image: Zib immediately reconnects institutional victory to the mundane repair need that started the arc.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Later, Pixa's notification tone sounds once in operations and the nearest screen draws everyone's attention.
PANEL 2 — STATION STATUS: ACTIVE appears first, followed by ADAPTIVE OPERATIONS / INCIDENTAL MATERIAL OBSERVATION.
PANEL 3 — OUTPUT TARGET: NONE / BEHAVIORAL CONDITIONS: NONE / PROCUREMENT: OPERATIONS PRIORITY completes the decision.
PANEL 4 — Astra reads in silence long enough for Zib to ask the only question he cares about: whether active comes with a bracket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Central review has returned its decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: We're still active?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Adaptive operations approved. Incidental material observation retained. No output target.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Does 'active' come with an actual bracket?

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the abstract approval changes something concrete. Middle image: the crew reacts in character rather than celebrating generically. Closing image: the temporary repair's end becomes a comic future problem.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back at the open bracket panel, Pixa checks procurement and the replacement ETA has collapsed to two days.
PANEL 2 — Zib stares at the screen and calls the sudden generosity suspicious.
PANEL 3 — Astra finally smiles and tells him not to investigate procurement generosity; Brick opens his notebook anyway.
PANEL 4 — Jax looks at the temporary tag and jokes that they may have to learn what permanent means while Glorp objects from nearby.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Replacement part due in two days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: That was fast. Suspiciously fast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Do not investigate the one good thing procurement has done for us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: Too late.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: What are we supposed to do with a permanent part? We've become attached to temporary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: I can show you the difference in the maintenance register.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the season's negotiated boundaries become routine paperwork. Middle image: the vending-machine joke survives institutional resolution. Closing image: Astra is already carrying ordinary work into whatever comes next.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Later in operations, Glorp and Kreeb build the durable reporting template for the approved program; BEHAVIORAL CONTEXT is visibly marked NOT REQUIRED.
PANEL 2 — Kreeb calls the deliberate blank space intentional while, across the room, the vending machine prints STATION STATUS: ACTIVE and Brick turns toward it.
PANEL 3 — Astra walks past carrying ordinary work orders and calls the new normal normal enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Behavioral context: not required. I never expected a form to make me feel so free.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: You're coming over tonight, aren't you? Everybody's playing. Pixa too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: I'm bringing the cards. Your set has the wrong scoring instructions.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: You'd enjoy the game if you stopped treating the scores like evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: The vending machine has printed our station approval. A curious witness.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Normal enough. And for once, Glorp, knock on the door when you get there.
